genxml.title: Bedrock network interface (NI) registers: field layouts, port error bits and routing tables
genxml.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
genxml.doc: Offsets are in the node's local alias, the same offsets the census names in devices/bedrock/registers.toml. Register names, offsets, widths and field positions come from the public Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers, read directly from that tag, so they are established as header facts. Behaviour the headers give only in their comments is inferred. No Bedrock specification is held. The headers state no reset value, so every reset is unknown, except one software default the headers name without a source.

struct.name: PORT_STATUS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Link-level protocol status. The header calls bit 1 link up and bit 2 remote power; the header gives no encoding for the two-bit status, so the meaning of bit 1 is inferred from its name.

struct.name: PORT_RESET
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Writing this register resets the network interface. The header's comments say bit 0 sends a link reset to the peer, bit 1 sends a warm reset over the link and bit 2 resets the local Bedrock. What the peer does with a link reset is not stated. Reset unknown.

struct.name: RESET_ENABLE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Warm reset enable. The header's comment says bit 0 lets a reset arriving over the link reset the Bedrock. The header does not say whether the bit also gates a local reset, so that is unknown.

struct.name: DIAG_PARMS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Diagnostic parameters. Field names are the header's; the header gives no operating description beyond them.

struct.name: CHANNEL_CONTROL
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Virtual channel selection for outgoing messages. Bits 0 to 3 pick the channel for requests of each class and bits 4 to 7 for replies.

struct.name: CHANNEL_TEST
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Access to the link test logic: seed, mask, data, valid, error and flit fields, plus clear and error-capture controls. The header gives the field layout only. Reset unknown.

struct.name: PORT_PARMS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Link-level protocol parameters and the enables for error header capture. The header gives field positions, and the reset-defaults constant above.

struct.name: CHANNEL_AGE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Age at which request and reply packets enter the fabric. The header's comment says a higher reply age gives replies fixed priority over requests under saturation (inferred from the comment).

struct.name: PORT_ERRORS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Latched link-port and problem-message errors. The header's comment says reads do not change the register and bits 52 to 24 assert the network interface interrupt (inferred from the comment). The header's comment says the eight-bit counters do not wrap.

struct.name: PORT_HEADER_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: First half of the header of an erroring packet, as the header's union lays it out. The header's comment says it holds the captured header. Reset unknown.

struct.name: PORT_HEADER_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Second half of the header of an erroring packet, as the header's union lays it out. Reset unknown.

struct.name: PORT_SIDEBAND
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Sideband data for the header registers and extra error data. The header says this register is not cleared on reset. Its write effect is not stated, so the access direction is taken from the header's description as data the port provides.

struct.name: PORT_ERROR_CLEAR
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: The same information as port errors, with the same layout. The header's comment for this register repeats the port-errors comment, including that reads are non-destructive, which conflicts with the register name. The read effect is therefore unknown: the header does not settle whether a read clears the latched errors. Whether the read clears anything is unknown.

struct.name: LOCAL_TABLE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Next-hop table for a local destination, one entry per 7-bit local destination at a stride of eight bytes; entry 0 is at the base. The header names the table and gives no access direction.

struct.name: GLOBAL_TABLE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Next-hop table for the one-bit meta destination. The header names the table and gives no access direction.
